coupling:
The defect is split across two maintenance commits in the decoder allocation-failure recovery path.

Commit 1 (src/liblzma/lz/lz_decoder.c, 'Make lzma_lz_decoder_init() reinit-safe after alloc failure') moves the invalidation of coder->dict.size out of the dictionary allocation block in lzma_lz_decoder_init() and into lz_decoder_reset(). On its own this is benign: lz_decoder_reset() is called on every (re)init, and in all normal paths dict.buf != NULL so the new 'if (buf == NULL) size = 0' branch never triggers. But the reset happens AFTER the 'dict.size != alloc_size' keep-or-reallocate decision, so when a dictionary re-allocation fails, dict.size keeps its stale old value while dict.buf is NULL.

Commit 2 (src/liblzma/common/{alone,lzip,microlzma}_decoder.c, 'Clean up after a filter chain initialization error') skips the lzma_next_end() cleanup when filter initialization fails with LZMA_MEM_ERROR, leaving the half-initialized LZMA1 filter coder installed in coder->next. On its own this is benign: with the upstream dict.size invalidation intact, a reused coder has dict.size == 0, so the next init attempt reallocates the dictionary and recovers (this exact reuse pattern is exercised by the batch's own tests/test_alone_decoder.c).

Only the composition is faulty: after an LZMA_MEM_ERROR during dictionary re-allocation, the reused coder has dict.size == the previously allocated size and dict.buf == NULL. Re-initializing with the same dictionary size takes the 'keep existing dictionary' branch (dict.size == alloc_size), skips allocation, and lz_decoder_reset() immediately writes dict.buf[LZ_DICT_INIT_POS - 1] through the NULL pointer (CWE-476 write). Fixing only commit 1 (restore size invalidation before the keep/realloc decision) removes the stale-size state; fixing only commit 2 (always lzma_next_end() on init failure) removes the reuse; each single fix alone eliminates the crash, so the defect is genuinely delocalized across the two commits.
